proposal: 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude (776BC), 30 September 2026, v1.0
consent: I approve the 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude proposal dated 30 September 2026: up to 20 hours of implementation and a four-week controlled pilot for a fixed fee of A$5,000 ex GST, payable 50% on approval and commencement and 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot.
scope: Up to 20 hours of Claude Skill implementation over two weeks, followed by a four-week controlled pilot
payment_milestones: 50% on approval and commencement; 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot
approval_type: Approval of the proposal, including its stated scope, fixed fee and payment terms
proposal_text: 01 Purpose Following your review of 776BC’s approach to AI-supported copywriting, I recommend adapting the proposed Calliope pilot into a native Claude Skill. The objective is to give the 776BC team a simple, repeatable way to create and review selected content inside Claude while protecting the human authorship that underpins the authenticity of the brand. This revised approach removes the need for an external Telegram, Slack or Teams interface. Instead, the capability will operate directly within Claude as a dedicated 776BC Content & Copy Skill. The commercial investment remains unchanged. The effort previously allocated to external access and channel integration will instead be directed towards brand-canon preparation, authorship controls, skill development, evaluation and team deployment. Recommended decision Approve the 20-hour Claude Skill implementation and controlled pilot. Engagement parameters PlatformClaudeNative Skill Build period2 weeks Controlled pilot4 weeks Effort20 hours Fixed feeA$5,000ex GST Revision note This proposal replaces the Calliope Telegram Pilot proposal dated 4 September 2026. 02 Project objective Design, build and deploy a production-ready Claude Skill that: Reviews copy against the approved 776BC brand canon Produces website, print collateral and social copy Protects campaign, blog and article content as human-authored categories Gives users clear, practical and prioritised editorial advice Distinguishes between content it may create and content it may only review Requires human approval before any output is published Can be installed and used by nominated 776BC team members within Claude Content marking The Skill will not attempt to remove, alter or circumvent Claude’s content-marking mechanisms. 03 Proposed capability The user will access one clear capability within Claude: 776BC Content & Copy Skill The Skill will identify the type of content being requested and apply the appropriate operating mode. Content typeReview permittedCreation permittedRewriting permitted Website copyYesYesYes Campaign copyYesNoNo Print collateralYesYesYes Social copyYesYesYes Blogs and articlesYesNoNo Ambiguous requests Where a request is ambiguous, the Skill will seek clarification or default to the more conservative review-only mode. Copy review The Skill will assess submitted copy against the 776BC brand canon and provide: An overall assessment Brand-alignment scoring Strengths to preserve Issues ranked by importance Prohibited or off-brand language Unsupported or potentially risky claims Structural and editorial guidance Questions for the human writer A recommendation on readiness for approval For campaigns, blogs and articles, Claude will act as a critic rather than a co-writer. It will diagnose and advise without returning publishable replacement copy. Approved copywriting For website, collateral and social content, the Skill will be permitted to create and revise copy. It will use the approved brand canon, relevant source material and the user’s brief to produce channel-appropriate drafts. Generated outputs will remain subject to human review and approval. 04 Implementation approach This is not simply the creation of a general prompt. The existing 776BC vault contains substantial brand intelligence, including voice principles, writing rules, vocabulary, prohibited language, storytelling structures, audience knowledge and existing Calliope instructions. That material must be assessed, curated and translated into a focused Claude capability. The complete vault should not be transferred wholesale into the Skill. Only the information required for the agreed use cases will be included. The work will be delivered across six workstreams. Workstream 1Effort: 2 hours Confirm the authorship policy A focused working session will confirm: The five content classifications Boundaries between website and campaign copy How campaign landing pages should be treated What Claude may and may not do when reviewing human-authored work Whether grammar corrections are permitted in review-only categories Approval responsibilities Initial users and representative test cases Workstream 2Effort: 4 hours Prepare the approved brand knowledge The current canon will be reviewed and a controlled content subset prepared for the Skill. This will include the brand guidance required to govern: Voice and tone Writing style Storytelling structure Approved vocabulary Prohibited terms Commercial restraint Audience respect Product and performance claims Channel-specific behaviour This process will also identify conflicting, duplicated or outdated instructions that could produce inconsistent results. Workstream 3Effort: 6 hours Design and build the Claude Skill The Skill will be configured to: Recognise relevant requests Classify the content type Apply the appropriate authorship rule Select the correct review or creation behaviour Reference the approved canon Ask only for material missing information Return content in consistent, usable formats Explain when and why a request has been limited Preserve mandatory human review The detailed instruction structure, internal decision logic and implementation method will be developed during delivery and are not reproduced in this proposal. Workstream 4Effort: 4 hours Evaluation and refinement A representative evaluation set will be created to test: Website creation Collateral creation Social creation Campaign review Article review Ambiguous content requests Mixed requests containing permitted and restricted content Attempts to override the authorship policy Brand voice drift Prohibited language Unsupported claims Insufficient source material Testing will focus on both output quality and boundary behaviour. Material issues identified during evaluation will be corrected before pilot release. The evaluation framework and detailed test cases form part of the implementation methodology and will be developed during the engagement. Workstream 5Effort: 2 hours Deployment and handover The completed Skill will be packaged for installation within Claude. Handover will include: Production-ready Claude Skill package Approved brand reference set Installation instructions Short user guide Example invocation patterns Known limitations Ownership and version record Pilot feedback process Deployment will depend on the 776BC Claude account structure. Claude Team or Enterprise may support internal sharing or organisation-level publication. Individual accounts may require separate installation by each user. Workstream 6Effort: 2 hours Controlled pilot and final refinement The Skill will enter a four-week controlled pilot using real 776BC content tasks. Feedback will be collected around: Accuracy of content classification Usefulness of reviews Brand alignment Quality of generated copy Incorrect or overly restrictive behaviour Time saved User confidence Missing canon guidance The engagement includes up to two hours of consolidated refinement following the pilot. Feedback should be collected and prioritised before this work is undertaken. 05 Effort and timeline WorkstreamHours Authorship policy confirmation2 Brand-canon preparation4 Skill design and development6 Evaluation and refinement4 Deployment and handover2 Pilot refinement allowance2 Total20 hours Delivery sequence Week 1 Kick-off and policy confirmation Review and preparation of brand material Skill architecture Initial working version Week 2 Skill development Evaluation and refinement Installation and release Team handover Weeks 3 to 6 Controlled team pilot Feedback capture Consolidated final refinement Pilot review and recommendation The implementation will commence once the proposal is approved, the initial payment is received and the required Claude and source-material access is available. 06 Deliverables 776BC will receive: One user-facing 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude Review, website and collateral, and social-copy operating modes Encoded human-authorship policy Curated 776BC brand reference set Copy-review and scoring framework Evaluated production release Installation package User and administration guide Four-week controlled pilot Up to two hours of post-pilot refinement Recommended next steps following the pilot 07 Success criteria The pilot will be considered successful when: The Skill correctly identifies the agreed content categories across the release test set Campaigns, blogs and articles remain in review-only mode Website, collateral and social requests produce usable first drafts Hard-block brand-language violations are identified Reviews provide clear and actionable guidance The Skill reflects the approved 776BC voice and writing principles Nominated users can install and use the Skill reliably No content is published without human approval Human approval remains mandatory Claude Skills guide model behaviour rather than operating as a technically locked publishing system. Model outputs can vary between requests. Human approval therefore remains a mandatory part of the operating model. 08 Scope exclusions The following are not included in this engagement: Telegram, Slack or Microsoft Teams integration A separate Hermes or OpenClaw agent Social-media scheduling or publishing CMS integration or automated website publishing Creation of campaign copy, blogs or articles Full live access to the complete 776BC vault Modification of the existing Flowstate or Workbench platforms New n8n workflows Visual design or image generation Legal verification of marketing claims Claude subscription or account fees Ongoing content production Ongoing support beyond the included pilot refinement Any additional integration, content category or workflow will be scoped separately before work begins. 09 Investment Fixed project fee A$5,000 excluding GST The fee covers up to 20 hours of design, development, testing, deployment and included pilot refinement. Payment terms 50% on approval and commencement 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot Additional work requires prior written approval Approved additional work is billed at A$250 per hour excluding GST This proposal is valid for 14 days. 10 Intellectual property 776BC retains ownership of its existing brand material, source content and confidential business information. Following full payment, 776BC will receive an ongoing internal-use licence for the completed 776BC-specific Skill package, curated brand references and operating documentation. OptiFlows retains ownership of its pre-existing and reusable methods, frameworks, evaluation approaches, underlying templates, implementation techniques and general know-how. The completed Skill may be used internally by 776BC but may not be resold, redistributed or provided to third parties as a standalone product without written agreement. Detailed implementation logic, working materials and proprietary evaluation methods are produced as part of the engagement and are not transferred through this proposal document. 11 Recommended decision Approve the 20-hour Claude Skill implementation and controlled pilot. This provides 776BC with a contained and practical way to improve content quality and production efficiency while preserving the human authorship that gives the brand its credibility.
